entries.sanskrit:
दशमेऽपातयद् रिङ्गन्न् अन्तरा यमलार्जुनौ ।

तत्रत्याभ्यां च देवाभ्यां कृष्णः स्तुत इतीर्यते ॥॥

यद् विगर्हितं कर्म, येन वा देवर्षेर् भागवतोत्तमस्यापि तमः क्रोधः, तद् एतत् कथ्यताम् इति ॥१॥
word_for_word: by the two gods dwelling there
entries.literal_english: In the Tenth [Chapter] He knocked down the twin Arjuna trees while crawling, and Kṛṣṇa was praised by the two gods who had been dwelling there. Let the reprehensible act be told—the act by which even the darkness of anger arose in the exalted divine sage Nārada.

entries.literal_english: They were within the Ganges, in the midst of the river where there are rows of lotus groves.

entries.literal_english: He saw them, and by seeing them he understood that the two were intoxicated and maddened.

entries.sanskrit: अनुग्रहार्थाय अनुग्रहश् च मद-नाशोऽर्थश् च श्री-कृष्ण-दर्शनं तद् अर्थम् । इदं वक्ष्यमाणं न ह्य् अन्य इत्य्-आदि ॥७॥
entries.literal_english: The purpose was mercy: the destruction of their intoxication and the granting of Lord Kṛṣṇa’s audience. The passage that follows, beginning ‘for no other...’, explains this purpose.

entries.sanskrit: इमं नश्वरं देहम् अजरा-मृत्यु अजरश् च अमृत्युश् च यथा तथा मन्यमानैः ॥९॥
word_for_word: free from old age and death
entries.literal_english: They thought this perishable body to be free from old age and death, as though it were truly ageless and immortal.

entries.sanskrit: नर-देव-भूदेव संज्ञितम् अपि श्वादिभिर् भक्षितं विट्-संज्ञितं दग्धं भस्म-संज्ञितम् अन्यदा कृमि-संज्ञितम् । तत्-कृते तद्-अर्थं यो भूत-ध्रुक् भूत-द्रोग्धा । यतो भूत-द्रोहान् निरयो भवति स किं स्वार्थं वेद । नैव वेदेत्य् अर्थः ॥१०॥
entries.literal_english: The body may be designated a human king or an earthly god, yet it is eaten by dogs and others; it becomes what is called excrement, or is burned and becomes ashes, or becomes what is called worms. One who harms living beings for the sake of that body—does he know his own good, when hell results from such harm? He certainly does not.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: इदानीं देहेऽहं भावोऽपि न घटत इत्य् आह---देह इति । निषेक्तुः पितुः । मातुः पितुर् वा माताम् अहस्य पुत्रिका-करणे ॥११॥
word_for_word: of the one who emitted the seed
in making [the child] a daughter’s son
entries.literal_english: He now says that even the idea ‘I am the body’ does not stand consistently. The body might be claimed by the father who supplied the seed, by the mother, or by the maternal grandfather when the child is made his daughter’s son; the text thus begins to expose the uncertainty of bodily ownership.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अव्यक्त-प्रभवाप्ययम् अव्यक्तात् प्रभवस् तस्मिन्न् एवाप्ययो यस्य तम् आत्म-सात्-कृत्वा आत्मेति मत्वा । असतो मूढाद् ऋते ॥१२॥
word_for_word: whose origin and dissolution are in the unmanifest
entries.literal_english: The body has its origin in the unmanifest and returns to the unmanifest. Who, except a foolish person, would claim such a body as the self, thinking ‘this is my ātman’?
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: एवं श्री-मद-विचेष्टितम् उक्त्वा तत् प्रतीकारं निश्चिनोति---असत इति । परं श्रेष्ठं, दारिद्र्यम् एव केवलम् इति वा । कुत इत्य् अत आह---आत्मौपम्येनेति । ततो न द्रुह्यतीति भावः ॥१३॥
word_for_word: the conduct of one blinded by wealth
entries.literal_english: Having described the conduct of one blinded by wealth, he determines the remedy: poverty—indeed, poverty alone, or the supreme poverty. Why? Through comparison with himself, the poor person sees the suffering of living beings and therefore does not harm them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: स-दृष्टान्तम् आह---यथेति । मुखाम्लान्यादि-लिङ्गैः सर्वेषां जीवानां सुख-दुःखे समे इति ज्ञातवान् इत्य् अर्थः ॥१४॥
word_for_word: one whose body is pierced by a thorn
by signs such as faces becoming cheerless
entries.literal_english: He gives an example. Just as one whose body has been pierced by a thorn understands another’s pain, so by signs such as the change in facial expression he understands that pleasure and pain are alike in all living beings.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, दारिद्र्यं मोक्षम् अपि साधयतीत्य् आह---दरिद्र इति श्लोक-चतुष्टयेन । निरहं-स्तम्भो निर्गतोऽहङ्कार-रूपः स्तम्भो यस्मात् सः ॥१५॥
entries.literal_english: Moreover, he says through these four verses that poverty can assist even liberation. The poor person is free from the pride that arises from the ego.

entries.literal_english: Saintly persons spontaneously associate with the poor. Through that association the thirst of material craving is diminished.

entries.sanskrit: ननु साधूनाम् अपि धनिकः प्रियः स्यान् न दरिद्र इति तत्राह---साधूनाम् इति । धनेन स्तम्भो गर्वो येषां तैः ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: One might object that a wealthy person could also be dear to saintly persons, rather than a poor person. He answers: those who possess wealth are afflicted by the pride and arrogance produced by it.

entries.sanskrit: शपति, अतोऽर्हत इति । अनुगृह्णाति, स्यातां नैवम् इत्य्-आदिना । मत्-प्रसादेन स्मृतिः स्यात् ॥२१॥
entries.literal_english: He curses them because they deserve it, and he also bestows mercy, saying ‘May it not remain so.’ By My grace, remembrance will arise in them.

entries.sanskrit: स्वर्-लोकतां देवत्वं पुनर् लब्ध्वा मद्-अनुग्रहाल् लब्ध-भक्ती भविष्यत इति ॥२२॥
word_for_word: the status of the heavenly world
entries.literal_english: They will again obtain the status of the heavenly world and divine bodies; by My mercy they will become endowed with devotion.

entries.sanskrit: किम् इति सत्यं कर्तव्यं तत्राह---देवर्षिर् इति । यद् यतः । तत् ततः ॥२५॥
entries.literal_english: Why should this be done? He answers: it must be made true because the speaker is the divine sage Nārada; what he says therefore comes to pass.

entries.sanskrit: यमयोर् यमलयोः सहजातयोः । आत्मनः कृष्णस्य तन्-मध्य-प्रवेश-मात्रेण ॥२६॥
word_for_word: merely by His entering between them
entries.literal_english: ‘The twins’ means the two born together. The trees were freed merely by Kṛṣṇa Himself entering between them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अनु अञ्चतीत्य् अन्वक् । तत्र हेतुः, दामोदरेणेति । उत्कलितः उत्पाटितोऽङ्घ्रि-बन्धो मूल-बन्धो ययोस् तौ । परमस्य श्री-कृष्णस्य विक्रमितं विक्रमस् तेनाति-वेपः कम्पो येषु ते स्कन्ध-प्रवाल-विटपा ययोस् तौ ॥२७॥
word_for_word: the binding of the feet / root-bond
entries.literal_english: ‘Following’ means coming after Him. The trees’ root-bond was uprooted by Dāmodara, and their trunks, shoots and branches trembled intensely from the force of the Supreme Lord Kṛṣṇa’s movement.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: ककुभः प्रति सर्वतः स्फुरन्ताव् इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, दिशः प्रकाशयन्ताव् इति । कुजयोर् वृक्षयोः स्थितोऽग्निर् यथा मूर्तिम् आनुपैति तथोपेत्य । विरजसौ निर्मदौ निरहङ्कारिणौ नष्ट-गर्वाव् इति यावत् ॥२८॥
entries.literal_english: They shone forth toward all directions, illuminating them. As fire assumes a visible form, the two beings emerged from the trees; they were free from passion, free from intoxication, and free from pride.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: गोपालं मां युवां देवौ किम् इति प्रणताव् इति चेत् तत्राहतुः, हे कृष्ण कृष्ण महा-योगिन्, अचिन्त्य-प्रभावस् त्वं न गोपालः, किन्तु परः पुरुषः । यत आद्यः कारण-भूतः । तत्रापि न निमित्त-मात्रं किन्तूपादानम् अपि त्वम् एवेत्य् आशयेन तुष्टुवतुः, व्यक्ताव्यक्तम् इति । स्थूल-सूक्ष्मम् इदं ते रूपं विदुः ॥२९॥
entries.literal_english: If someone asks, ‘Why do you two bow to me, a cowherd?’, they answer: ‘O Kṛṣṇa, O great yogin of inconceivable power, You are not merely a cowherd but the Supreme Person, the primordial cause. You are not only the instrumental cause; You are also the material cause. Thus they praise You as both manifest and unmanifest.’
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: नियन्तापि त्वम् एवेत्य् ऊचतुः, त्वम् एक इति । देहः, असवः प्राणाः, आत्माऽहङ्कारः, इन्द्रियाणि च तेषाम् ईश्वरः । नन्व् अस्य कालो निमित्तं प्रकृतिर् उपादानं प्रकृतेर् जातो महान् विश्वात्मतया परिणमते पुरुषः कर्ता नियन्ता च किम् अत्राहम् अत आहतुः, त्वम् एव काल इत्य्-आदिना सार्धेन । यतो भगवान् ईश्वरो विष्णुस् त्वम् अतः कालो नाम तव लीला ॥३०॥
entries.literal_english: You alone are the body, the life-breaths, the self, the ego, the senses and their Lord. Although time may be called the instrumental cause and primordial nature the material cause, You alone are also time and nature: as the Lord, You are the controller of all.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: प्रकृतिः शक्तिः, पुरुषोंऽशः, महान् कार्यम्, अतस् त्वम् एव सर्वम् इत्य् अर्थः ॥३१॥
entries.literal_english: Nature is Your energy, the person is Your portion, and the great principle is Your effect. Therefore everything is You.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: नन्व् अहम् एव चेत् सर्वं तर्हि घटादि-ज्ञाने मज्-ज्ञानं किं न भवति, भवतीति चेत् सर्वोऽपि ब्रह्म-वित् स्याद् अत आहतुः, गृह्यमाणैर् इति । दृश्यत्वेन वर्तमानैर् बुद्ध्य्-अहङ्कारेन्द्रियादिभिर् द्रष्टा त्वं न गृह्यसे इति भावः । ननु तर्हि जीवो जानातु नैवेत्य् आहतुः, को न्व् इहेति । जीवाद्य्-उत्पत्तेः प्राग् एव स्व-प्रकशतया सिद्धं त्वां को वा जानाति । गुण-सम्बृतो देहाद्य्-आवृतः ॥३२॥
word_for_word: by intellect, ego, senses and so on
entries.literal_english: If You alone are everything, why does knowledge of You not arise when a pot and other objects are known? They answer: as the seer, You are not grasped by intellect, ego, senses and the other instruments that are themselves objects of perception. And who could know You? You are self-luminous even before the creation of the individual soul, yet the body and its covering by the guṇas conceal You.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अतो दुर्ज्ञेयत्वात् केवलं प्रणमतः, तस्मै तुभ्यम् इति । आत्मनः स्वस्मात् द्योतः प्रकाशो येषां तैर् गुणैश् छन्नो महिमा यस्य । अभ्रैर् इव रवेस् तस्मै ॥३३॥
word_for_word: because of being difficult to know
entries.literal_english: Because You are difficult to know, we simply bow to You. Your greatness is covered by the guṇas, just as the sun’s radiance is covered by clouds.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: अहोऽहम् ईश्वर इति कुतो ज्ञानं तत्राहतुः, यस्येति ॥३४॥
entries.literal_english: How could the knowledge ‘I am the Lord’ arise? The two answer with the words ‘from whom...’, pointing to the source from which such knowledge could come.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: भवायोद्भवाय । विभवाय विगतो भवो यस्मिंस् तस्मै । कैवल्यायेत्य् अर्थः ॥३५॥
entries.literal_english: ‘For coming into being’ means for arising; ‘for freedom from becoming’ means for Him in whom worldly becoming has ceased. The intended meaning is absolute liberation.

entries.sanskrit: नौ आवाम् । अनुचरः कुबेरो नारदो वा तस्य किङ्करौ । भगवतस् तव दर्शनम् ॥३७॥
entries.literal_english: We two were attendants—servants of Kubera, or servants of Nārada. By Your mercy we have obtained the sight of the Lord.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: तत्र गतयोर् अवयोः पूर्व-स्वभावो विषय-प्रवणता इत्य्-आदि भवतु । न इत् बहु-वचनम् । अस्मदो द्वयोश् च [पा। १.२.५९] इति द्वि-वचन-स्थाने बहु-वचनम् । अस्मत्-सङ्गिनां सर्वेषाम् अपीति वा बहु-वचनम् । तव निवास-भूतं यज् जगत् तस्य प्रणामे । त्वन्-निवास-भूतम् इति बहु-मानेन जगतः प्रणामे शिरोस् त्व् इत्य् अर्थः । भवत्-तनूनां भवतो मूर्तीनाम् ॥३८॥
word_for_word: the universe that is Your abode
entries.literal_english: May our former nature, the tendency toward sense objects, now be gone. The plural may refer to all who are connected with us, or to the many forms of the Lord. We bow our heads to the universe that is Your abode and to Your divine forms.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: सङ्कीर्तितः संस्तुतः ॥३९॥
entries.literal_english: ‘Sankīrtita’ means praised or celebrated.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: वाग्भिः, न ह्य् अन्यो जुषतो जोष्यान् [भा।पु। १०.१०.८] इत्य्-आदिभिः । श्री-विभ्रंश-रूपो ऽनुग्रहः कृत इति ॥४०॥
word_for_word: in the form of loss of wealth
entries.literal_english: They praise Him with words such as ‘There is no other enjoyer of what is to be enjoyed.’ The Lord’s mercy has been bestowed in the form of their loss of wealth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: युक्तम् एवैतद् इत्य् आह---साधूनां स्व-धर्म-वर्तिनां सम-चित्तानाम् आत्म-विदां सुतरां मत्-कृतात्मनां मय्य् अर्पित-चित्तानाम् । तेषां कृपातिरेकात् सुतराम् इत्य् उक्तम् । सवितुर् दर्शनाद् अक्ष्णोर् यथा बन्धो न भवेत्, तद्वत् ॥४१॥
word_for_word: whose selves are offered to Me
because of an excess of compassion
entries.literal_english: This is appropriate: saintly persons follow their duty, are equal-minded, know the self, and have offered their very selves to Me. The phrase ‘especially’ indicates their abundant compassion. Their association does not bind the eyes, just as looking at the sun does not bind the eyes when one is prepared for its light.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; source range preserved. Source-backed lexical row audit completed.

entries.sanskrit: प्राधान्याद् एकस्य सम्बोधनम् । हे नलकूवर, युवां तत् तस्मात् सादनं स्व-निकेतं मत्-परमौ सन्तौ गच्छतम् । वां युवयोर् अपेक्षितो मयि प्रेमा जात एव । अभवः न भवो यस्मिन् सः ॥४२॥
word_for_word: with Me as your supreme goal
entries.literal_english: ‘O Nalakūvara, you two may go to your own abode, with Me as your supreme goal.’ The love for Me that you sought has already arisen in you. ‘Abhava’ means that in which worldly becoming is absent.
